clue.text: Dickie's pups are wild to choose playmates

indicators.note: puppies that are wild run riot, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A child's puppies run riot while the children pick teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are wild' rearranges all eleven letters of DICKIES PUPS, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: Picking sides is the playground ritual where captains take turns selecting team members.

clue.text: An introduction to Walker's Guide?

parts.note: a walker's guide might begin with something before an amble, a stroll

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's halves as 'before a stroll', a fitting opening for a walking guide.
explanation.definitionFit: An introductory statement opens a document, such as the opening of a constitution.

clue.text: Measuring the heat it changes to real crime

definitions.note: describes the job of a device, so it stands for the instrument

indicators.note: the following letters change their order to form the device

explanation.surface: A detective's heat gauge apparently turns crime real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a link pointing to the device; 'changes' rearranges TO REAL CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: This laboratory instrument quantifies the heat given off in chemical reactions or combustion.

clue.text: A French head of silver, antique, without a buyer

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: something antique is old

explanation.surface: An antique French silver head goes unbought at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods left with no purchaser remain on the shelf after a sale.

clue.text: Fires the containers

explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone is to dismiss them from work; large bags of coarse cloth hold coal or potatoes.

clue.text: A stupid fellow in charge of an engine?

definitions.note: describes a person, a worker who tends a ship's auxiliary engine

parts.note: a donkey is a stupid person, an ass
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A foolish chap is put in charge of machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: A donkey engine is a small auxiliary steam engine on a ship; its attendant has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: On a steamship the crewman who works the auxiliary engine in the engine room has this job title.

clue.text: Only minor cuts

parts.note: minor cuts sound like small wounds, but here they are small bits clipped out of a text

explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' suggests injuries; it means small pieces snipped off, as from news or music.
explanation.definitionFit: Small extracts or fragments cut from a larger piece, such as news items.

clue.text: A blade that's put in uninvited

explanation.definitionFit: A rowing blade is this; and the idiom 'put your oar in' means offering an unwanted opinion or interference.

clue.text: Part of a kimono binder

indicators.note: the letters needed are a part of the run across these words

explanation.surface: A garment fastening described as one component of Japanese dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the sash that binds a kimono and also contains it across 'kimono binder'.
explanation.definitionFit: The broad sash tied around a kimono's waist holds it closed.

clue.text: Did his, ears burn, during moon-landing transmissions?

definitions.text: Did his, ears burn, during moon-landing transmissions?

parts.words: Did his, ears burn, during moon-landing transmissions
parts.note: ears burn when people talk about you, and astronauts' radio messages kept saying a man's name meaning 'message received'

explanation.walkthrough: Radio users say a man's name to mean 'received and understood', so a man of that name would hear himself mentioned constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure this name signals that a message has been received and understood.

clue.text: New York's island is a length in front

indicators.note: the length piece is placed ahead of the other word

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: Describing an island off New York that juts out a length ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The ELL was an old English cloth measure of 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: The island in New York harbour was the immigration station where millions of arrivals were processed.

clue.text: A little shut eye in the permissive society

definitions.text: A little shut eye in the permissive society

parts.words: A little shut eye in the permissive society
parts.note: 'shut eye' suggests a nap, but read it as turning a blind eye, winking at misconduct as a tolerant society does

explanation.walkthrough: The verb comes from Latin for closing the eyes; its English sense is pretending not to see wrongdoing, which 'shut eye' points at rather than sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretly allowing wrongdoing by looking the other way is the core sense, like a permissive society tolerating misdeeds.

clue.text: Sally's home game ?

parts.note: the old song says Sally lives in 'our alley', and an alley is also a large glass ball in this children's game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally in our Alley' is an old English song; an alley is also a type of glass ball used in the game, so Sally's home names a piece of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's game is played by flicking small glass balls, one kind of which is called an alley.

clue.text: A paper ruler?

parts.note: a large paper size bears the name of a supreme monarch, so a ruler can be made of paper

explanation.walkthrough: Traditional British paper sizes carried names such as foolscap and crown; the largest was named after a supreme sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: The supreme sovereign of an empire is a ruler, and the same name was given to the largest traditional sheet size.

clue.text: Weird R.U.R. men begin counting again — from the left?

indicators.note: something weird is strange or twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Robots from Capek's play R.U.R. begin a recount, politically from the left.
explanation.walkthrough: R.U.R. is Karel Capek's play that introduced robots; 'Weird' rearranges its letters with MEN BEGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Assigning new numbers or doing a recount means numbering a series a second time.

clue.text: Limp sort of material?

explanation.definitionFit: Limping describes a disabled gait; lamé is a fabric woven with metallic thread.

clue.text: Sulphurous butterfly ?

parts.note: an old word for sulphur is also the name of a yellow butterfly, so the insect is 'sulphurous' by name

explanation.walkthrough: The old name for sulphur, as in 'fire and ...', is shared by a sulphur-yellow British butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow-winged Gonepteryx rhamni is named after the old biblical word for sulphur.

clue.text: Gives Jolson a second audition for a try-out

parts.note: with 'Gives' before it, giving a second audition is what someone who rehears an act does
Al Jolson was the American singer of The Jazz Singer

explanation.surface: Al Jolson gets called back for a second audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives' sets the verb's form, so the second audition supplies REHEARS; Jolson's first name follows, and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice performance before the real thing is a trial run.

clue.text: Portia's spot of mercy?

parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice Portia says mercy drops like gentle rain from heaven, so a drop of it is a small bit of rain

explanation.walkthrough: Portia's speech: 'The quality of mercy is not strain'd, It droppeth as the gentle rain from heaven'.
explanation.definitionFit: A single falling drop of water from a shower is what a spot of mercy is, in Portia's image.

clue.text: Stretch out for a pamphlet

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.definitionFit: To prolong or extend something in time is to drag it out.

clue.text: A teetotaller in pain is binding

parts.note: TT is the standard abbreviation for a teetotaller, one who abstains from drink
being in pain is to be aching

explanation.surface: A non-drinker suffering is apparently bound up.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastening or binding something on is a synonym for joining it to another thing.

clue.text: Poet without aspiration has a measure of Hebrew

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy H sound, so the letter H is dropped

parts.note: Homer is the Greek epic poet of the Iliad

explanation.surface: A poet who has lost his breath carries a Hebrew measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without aspiration' removes the H (the aspirate) from HOMER; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An omer is a Hebrew dry measure of grain mentioned in Exodus.

clue.text: Start out to show to advantage

explanation.definitionFit: To set off is to begin a journey; it also means to enhance by contrast, as a frame does a picture.

clue.text: There was a strange drama in her stormy life

definitions.text: There was a strange drama in her stormy life

indicators.note: something strange is odd or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heroine whose life was a strange, tempestuous drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines Prospero's daughter in Shakespeare's The Tempest, whose life began with a storm; 'strange' rearranges DRAMA IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero's daughter in The Tempest grows up on an island after a shipwreck, her story set amid a storm.

clue.text: Dr. Ben's old Indian coin?

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
Ben's surname partner is Hur, from the film Ben-Hur

explanation.surface: A doctor's collection includes an old Indian coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben-Hur is the novel and film of the chariot race; Hur completes Ben.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold coin of Mughal and British India, worth fifteen rupees.

clue.text: Give over, now

explanation.definitionFit: To present is to hand over formally; the present is the current time.

clue.text: Finish with snap judgment on race problems

definitions.text: Finish with snap judgment on race problems

parts.words: Finish with snap judgment on race problems
parts.note: a snap, a picture taken by camera, decides close races; put before finish it names that judging method

explanation.walkthrough: A close race is settled by a picture at the line: the word before 'finish'. A snap is a quick picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal camera picture, the kind used to decide close finishes.

clue.text: What the rabbit-producer has to say!

definitions.text: What the rabbit-producer has to say!

parts.words: What the rabbit-producer has to say
parts.note: a rabbit-producer is a stage conjuror pulling a rabbit from a hat, who utters a magic exclamation

explanation.walkthrough: The rabbit-producer is not a breeder but a conjuror.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's triumphant exclamation as a trick is revealed.

clue.text: A tree where the river rises

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads the word upwards, so its letters are turned around

parts.note: the Wey is a river in Surrey, a tributary of the Thames

explanation.surface: Locating a tree at a river's source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' is a link; 'rises' turns WEY upwards in this down entry. The Wey is a river in Surrey, south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen conifer common in English churchyards.

clue.text: Board's bilingual assent

parts.note: oui is the French word for yes
ja is the German word for yes

explanation.surface: A board agreeing in two languages at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The talking board used at seances takes its name from yes in two languages.
explanation.definitionFit: The lettered spirit board used at seances is known by this trade name.

clue.text: Use 7 across for a quarrel

explanation.definitionFit: To use an oar is to propel a boat by it; a row is also a noisy argument.

clue.text: A thumping good featherweight contest!

parts.note: featherweight suggests a boxing class, but the weapons are feather-filled cushions used for thumping

explanation.walkthrough: 'featherweight' looks like boxing; the weight is literally feathers, inside bedroom cushions.
explanation.definitionFit: Children swinging soft bedroom cushions at each other wage this mock battle.
